resources.string: Preparation continues while you leave the app. You can cancel from the notification.
Image prepared and checked. Return to the app to select a USB target.
Preparation interrupted. Select the image and start again.
Android stopped preparation at its background time limit. Return to the app and start again.
Show the complete catalog without filtering by board.
Choose your Pi to filter the OS catalog. Compatibility follows the catalog information. Check local images yourself.
Changing the model clears the current image selection and first-boot settings. The cached file can be removed with Clear image and settings.
Search this category and its loaded subcategories. Open remote categories to search their contents.
No matching images. Clear the search, go back, or choose another model.
Write an operating system to a USB drive or SD card reader.
The image is still loading. The next step opens automatically afterwards.
Writing first-boot settings into the image…
IMG, ISO, XZ, GZ or ZIP from this device. Loading starts right after choosing.
Connect a USB-OTG card reader. Eject its mounted volumes in Android first.
All data on %1$s (%2$s) will be overwritten with %3$s. Double-check the device. Never disconnect it during writing or verification.
The entire device is overwritten. A complete read-back check follows automatically.
Keep the USB device connected. You can leave this screen while writing.
Cancelled. A partly written device must be imaged again.
USB access was denied. Select the device to try again.
USB-OTG required · No root · Android 8+\nFirst-boot settings require a supported FAT32 boot image. Connect setup uses an auth key. Secure boot is not available.

Applied to the prepared image before writing. Account passwords are hashed; Wi-Fi credentials and Connect keys are written to the boot partition. Settings stay in this app session. Clear the image to remove its cached copy.
Choose the format supported by your local image. No automatic detection is performed.
Public-key authentication requires at least one public key. Never paste a private key.
Enable Raspberry Pi hardware interfaces at first boot.
This image contains a single-use Connect key. For another Pi, create a new key and prepare the image again.
Link the Pi to your Raspberry Pi Connect account at first boot. Create an auth key in your browser, then paste it here.
This catalog image does not advertise Connect support. Choose a compatible Raspberry Pi OS image.
For local images, Connect must already be installed with its sign-in service. The app does not install packages. Lite supports remote shell; screen sharing needs a Wayland desktop.
No browser available. Open https://connect.raspberrypi.com/settings on another device.

Use a new key for each Pi. Personal keys expire after 6 hours; organisation keys use their chosen expiry. Boot with internet access before expiry. The key is readable in the prepared image and on its boot partition until consumed. Clear the image and settings after use.
Choose a supported first-boot format for this image.
The hostname must be a single name of 1–63 letters, digits or hyphens.
Choose a regular Linux username, not a system account.
The account password contains characters that cannot be used.
Set an account password or enable SSH with a public key.
The account password must have at least 8 characters.
Unknown timezone. Use a name such as Europe/Berlin.
The keyboard layout must be a Linux layout code such as de or us.
Choose a valid two-letter Wi-Fi country.
The Wi-Fi name must have 1–32 bytes and no control characters.
The Wi-Fi password needs 8–63 ASCII characters or a 64-digit hexadecimal key.
SSH password login requires an account password.
Add at least one SSH public key.
Passwordless sudo needs an account with a password or an SSH key.
Paste an OpenSSH public key, never a private key.
An SSH public key is not encoded correctly.
An SSH public key has an invalid length.
The type of an SSH public key does not match its contents.
Each SSH public key must be on a single line.
Paste a personal or organisation Connect auth key: rpuak_ or rpoak_ followed by 24 Base58 characters.
This catalog image does not advertise Raspberry Pi Connect support.
This image does not match the selected Raspberry Pi model.
This catalog entry contains no supported image.
The OS catalog could not be read. Try again later.
Only secure HTTPS downloads are supported.
The download server answered with HTTP %1$s. Try again later.
The download was redirected too often or without a target.
The downloaded image does not have the size given in the catalog.
This catalog image has no valid SHA-256 checksum and cannot be verified.
The image does not match its catalog checksum. Download it again.
Not enough free storage on this device for the unpacked image.
The chosen file cannot be opened.
The ZIP file contains no IMG or ISO file.
Reading the image stopped making progress. Choose it again.
The image could not be stored or removed in app storage.
The prepared image has changed. Load the image again.
The preparation is in an unexpected state. Load the image again.
Another image operation is still running.
First-boot settings need a Raspberry Pi image with a FAT32 boot partition.
The boot partition of this image cannot be edited safely.
The first-boot settings could not be verified on the boot partition.
A different USB device is connected now. Select it again.
Allow access to the USB device to continue.
This USB storage device is not supported.
The USB device cannot be opened.
The USB device is in use. Eject mounted drives in the Android settings first.
The USB transfer failed or timed out. Reconnect the device and try again.
There is no card in the USB reader.
The USB storage size has changed. Select the device again.
The image is larger than the USB device.
The prepared image ended unexpectedly. Load it again.
Verification failed at byte %1$s. The device must be written again.
No connection to the server. Check the internet connection and try again.
